• L’Antica Via del Cifalco is a mule track used since the Middle Ages by merchants, who travelled it to carry goods between the sea and the plain, but also by monks, brigands, soldiers, wayfarers, vagabonds and street performers, who peopled its woods, villages and inns.
  • From the emerald-coloured waters of the river Trebbia near Ponte Organasco (Piacenza, Emilia-Romagna) it leads to Portofino Mare (Genoa, Liguria) over about 75 kilometres and 2,800 metres of ascent (not counting any detours).
  • Through a project to enhance its hiking, historical and landscape value, it has recently been rediscovered: today it is open to the public along its entire length, on foot or by mountain bike (MTB).
  • The route, which winds along the entire ridge between the Trebbia and the Aveto, threads its way through villages brimming with history and legends.
  • It crosses an immense diversity of landscapes, embracing river, lake, woodland and mountain environments all the way down to the sea, thus dancing gently between the Apennines and the Mediterranean.
